slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
A regular n-gon inscribed in a circle of radius r splits into n isosceles triangles with apex angle 360/n at the center.

Each side is s = 2r sin(180/n), so the perimeter is P = 2nr sin(180/n).

Half of each isosceles triangle is a right triangle with hypotenuse r and angle 180/n at the center, so half a side is r sin(180/n). A regular hexagon has s = 2r sin 30 degrees = r, so its perimeter is 6r.
